name: Periwinkle Blue
lede: Periwinkle blue is a light purplish blue, the shade named after the periwinkle flower.

sections.title: A flower's blue
sections.body:
Paterson defines periwinkle as a purplish blue and periwinkle blue as a light purplish blue [1]. St Clair's glossary agrees on the flower: periwinkle there is a lilac-blue, named for the plant [2]. Paterson also lists *pervenche blue* beside it among the blues, a neighboring name for the same idea [3].

The books give no maker, pigment or date for the compound name [1][2][3]. In our library the earliest source that carries it is the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, which places the swatch in the brilliant purplish blue block [4]. The word periwinkle itself peaks in printed English in the 2010s [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #8F99FB sits between [[periwinkle]] and [[lavender]] in feel, bluer than the second and lighter than a true [[royal-blue]] [4]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 4 have it covering at least 5% of the canvas, among them Bonnard's *Vue panoramique, Le Cannet* of 1924 and Piero della Francesca's portrait of Battista Sforza [6]. Those are photographs of varnished paintings, so the colors are as photographed [6].
